<!-- pr-reviewer: 56f8faf0b2b692bcdbbd1fe0cae7a3af1e21436b -->
**Needs changes before merge.**

This is the delta review after the review at `5eb67ba20`. The two findings of that review are fixed. One quick-gate step is red on the new head.

**What looks good**

- Spot check depth. `spot_probes` compares the deepest claimed cell of each sampled item, then 8 fixed places. `want_at` evaluates every item over the probed cell. The probes are plain values, so the check reads the CPU law.
- Timeout latch. `CutError { kind, message }` and `CutErrorKind::NoAnswer` turn the latch into a value read. `map_wait_end` gives `NoAnswer` to the poll timeout and to a map wait that ends, and `Other` to a map that fails with an error. The latch no longer reads text.
- The four pins:
  - `an_edge_only_chord_is_checked_at_its_deepest_cell` puts the deepest cell at the brick edge and asserts that the centre cell stays at the floor. A centre-only check cannot find the wrong value.
  - `a_wrong_texel_at_a_fixed_lattice_place_fails_the_spot_check` puts a value at a fixed place that no item reaches.
  - `a_map_wait_that_ends_latches_the_gpu_off` and the lib test `the_read_back_wait_that_ends_is_a_no_answer` pin the kind, not the text.
  I read the diff and agree that each pin fails when its fix is reversed.
- The CPU twin does not change in this delta. `the_cpu_law_answers_the_sim_twin_bit_for_bit` is green.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()` in the non-test code of the diff. The decision doc paragraph matches the code. The PR body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #2627`. The commit subjects are conventional.

**Results merged with main** (locally, no runner; trial merge with `origin/main` `64b737729` is clean, no conflict; `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3`, debug)

| Binary | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft_sim:stock_cut_twin` | 8 passed |
| `camcraft_gpu:lib` | 7 passed |
| `camcraft_gpu:bin_parity` | 3 passed |
| `camcraft_gpu:cut_parity` | 9 passed |
| `camcraft_gpu:refusals` | 6 passed |

The four pins also ran alone with `--exact`: each 1 passed. A compute adapter was present; the tests that need one passed and none printed `SKIPPED`.

Clippy: `camcraft-sim --all-targets` is clean. `camcraft-gpu --lib --bins` is clean. `camcraft-gpu --all-targets` is red:

```
error: this operation has no effect
   --> crates/gpu/tests/cut_parity.rs:202:18
    |
202 |     let fixed = (1 * dy + 1) * dx + 1; // the quarter place, cell [1, 1, 1]
    |                  ^^^^^^ help: consider reducing it to: `dy`
    = note: `-D clippy::identity-op` implied by `-D warnings`
```

**Heavy lanes**: heavy not run - owed to the cut. The author's dry-run names `app heavy` and `motion heavy`.

**Requested before merge**

1. `crates/gpu/tests/cut_parity.rs:202` - `let fixed = (1 * dy + 1) * dx + 1;` fails the quick-gate clippy step with `-D warnings`. Change it to `let fixed = (dy + 1) * dx + 1;`. The test meaning does not change. Run `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` before the next head.

**Questions / notes** (not blocking)

- The spot check now costs up to 64 x 512 cell evaluations for the item probes, and up to 72 x items containment tests for each batch. The decision doc states this cost.
- A hardware adapter and a real timeout hang are still not exercised. The PR body says so. The claim margin and the spot check cover the adapter case.
- Label: `needs-rework`, because the quick gate clippy step is red. The PR stays a draft.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: eda43015d208d4064852d646713881b82a3cc5b6 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This is the delta re-check after the review at `56f8faf0b`. That review found one item: `clippy::identity_op` at `crates/gpu/tests/cut_parity.rs:202`. The item is fixed, and the readings are green on the new head.

## What looks good

- The fix is `let fixed = (1 * dy + 1) * dx + 1;` -> `let fixed = (dy + 1) * dx + 1;`. The two expressions have the same value, so the test meaning does not change. Clippy is now clean.
- The merge of `origin/main` `64b737729` (commit `fadf933b7`) is clean. Its `git show --remerge-diff` is empty: no hand edits in the merge. The full list of files that the PR adds against `origin/main` is the same one that the earlier reviews read: `crates/gpu/*`, `crates/sim/*` and `docs/decisions/2627-gpu-removal-kernel.md`. The merge brings main's changes only.
- The four pins are green on this head: `an_edge_only_chord_is_checked_at_its_deepest_cell`, `a_wrong_texel_at_a_fixed_lattice_place_fails_the_spot_check`, `a_map_wait_that_ends_latches_the_gpu_off` and `cut_gpu::tests::the_read_back_wait_that_ends_is_a_no_answer`.
- The PR body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #2627`. The commit subjects are conventional. The PR adds no `camcraft-*` dependency and changes no process file. No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()` is in the non-test code of the diff.

## Results merged with main

Locally, no runner. The tree is the head with the merge of `origin/main` `64b737729` already in it. `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=3`, debug.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |
| `camcraft_gpu:cut_parity` | 9 passed, 0 failed |
| `an_edge_only_chord_is_checked_at_its_deepest_cell` (`--exact`) | 1 passed |
| `a_wrong_texel_at_a_fixed_lattice_place_fails_the_spot_check` (`--exact`) | 1 passed |
| `a_map_wait_that_ends_latches_the_gpu_off` (`--exact`) | 1 passed |
| `cut_gpu::tests::the_read_back_wait_that_ends_is_a_no_answer` (`--exact`, lib) | 1 passed |

Clippy prints one warning about an unused workspace dependency (`truck-polymesh`). It comes from `Cargo.toml` on main and does not fail the check.

## Heavy lanes

Heavy not run - owed to the cut (P2, the new standard #3558). This delta changes one test line.

## Questions / notes

Not blocking. A hardware adapter and a real timeout hang stay unexercised. The PR body names this and the earlier reviews recorded it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
